Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
1227 AM PST Wed Nov 25 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Widespread coastal flooding is expected this week due to King 
Tides and increased surf. High clouds will spread across the area
today with not much change in high temperatures. For Thanksgiving
and Friday, offshore flow and strengthening high pressure aloft 
will bring warming with east to northeast winds gusting to 35 to 
45 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the mountains. 
Cooling will then spread inland for Saturday into next week. There
is a chance of showers for Sunday night and Monday with greater 
chances for stronger winds and heavier precipitation from a 
stronger storm some time around Tuesday and Wednesday of next 
week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

.SHORT TERM (Today through Friday)...
High clouds from a low pressure system moving inland to the north
will spread across the area today, clearing tonight. High 
temperatures for today will be similar to Tuesday. High
temperatures for today will be mostly in the 70s for the coast and
valleys, warmest for inland coastal areas into the western
valleys reaching the mid to upper 70s.

High pressure aloft and offshore lower-level flow will bring
warming for Thanksgiving and Friday with northeast to east winds 
gusting to 35 to 45 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the
mountains. High temperatures on Thanksgiving will warm 4 to 8
degrees, then another 5 degrees on Friday for the mountains and
high desert. High temperatures on Thanksgiving will be as much as
12 to 18 degrees above average for inland coastal areas into the 
western valleys, reaching the lower to mid 80s with not much 
change on Friday.

&&

.LONG TERM (Saturday through Tuesday)...
High clouds will increase again for Friday night and Saturday.
High pressure aloft will begin to weaken on Saturday and onshore
lower-level flow will return. High temperatures for the coast and
valleys will cool 4 to 8 degrees on Saturday with high
temperatures for the coast and valleys mostly in the mid 70s to
around 80. High temperatures will continue to cool through 
Tuesday with high temperatures for the coast and valleys on
Tuesday ranging from the mid 60s for the far inland valleys to 
around 70 for coastal areas.

A fast-moving low pressure system moving inland across California
on Sunday will bring a chance of showers for Sunday night and
Monday. A stormier pattern may develop across the Pacific into 
California for the rest of next week, but with lower confidence in
the timing and track of individual systems. A low pressure system
arriving some time around Tuesday and Wednesday could bring 
strong winds and heavy precipitation to southwestern California, 
but with lower confidence in the details. 

For Tuesday morning through Thursday night, the chance for 1 inch
or more of rainfall from the coast to the mountains ranges from 
75 to 85 percent for Orange and southwestern San Bernardino 
Counties, to around 60 percent across southern San Diego County. 
Chances for 3 inches or more of rainfall ranges from 5 to 10 
percent near the coast to 25 to 35 percent for the mountains.

&&

.AVIATION... 
250600Z...VFR prevailing. Increasing high clouds at/above 20,000 ft 
MSL and unrestricted VIS through Wednesday. Clouds clear Wednesday 
afternoon/evening. Northeast winds increase Wednesday afternoon and 
evening with gusts 25-35 kts below mountain passes.

&&

.MARINE...
No hazardous marine conditions are expected through early this 
morning.

A large, long period west swell will arrive this afternoon and 
build into Thursday, bringing combined seas of 8-12 feet. 
Additionally northwest winds may gust near 20 kts this afternoon 
in the far outer coastal waters. A Small Craft Advisory remains in
effect for the outer waters from late this morning through late 
Thursday morning due to the high seas. Seas begin to wane Thursday
afternoon, falling below 10 feet by Thursday evening.

&&

.BEACHES...
Record-breaking morning high tides this week. Highest tides each day 
through Thursday will be between 7.9-8.3 feet, peaking this 
morning. These forecast tides have been adjusted 1.1-1.2 feet 
above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent 
observations, and will likely break the all time tidal records 
just recently set in late October. 

Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet 
through this morning, but an incoming west swell of 7-8 ft at 
16-18 seconds arrives late today into Thursday. This will 
generate large breaking waves of 6-8 feet on Thursday, with sets 
of 10-12 feet on exposed west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-7 
feet on Friday. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for San 
Diego County for 1 PM Wednesday through 4 AM Friday with the swell
focusing the higher surf on the west-facing beaches.

The combination of forecast record King Tides and elevated to high 
surf will bring moderate to major coastal flooding, with locally 
extreme flooding expected during Thursday morning's high tide. A 
Coastal Flood Warning remains in effect this morning through early 
Friday afternoon.

&&

.CLIMATE...
The peak water level of 8.46 feet at the San Diego Broadway Pier 
on Tuesday morning was the second highest on record, exceeded only
by the 8.52 feet on October 27th of this year.

The peak water level of 7.97 feet at La Jolla on Tuesday morning 
was the second highest on record, exceeded narrowly and only by 
the 7.98 feet on October 27th of this year.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.

&&

.SGX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

     Coastal Areas-San Diego County Coastal Areas.

     High Surf Advisory from 1 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday 
     for San Diego County Coastal Areas.

PZ...Small Craft Advisory from 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST 
     Thursday for Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican 
     Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San Clemente 
     Island.
